target_customer: Small scale construction and renovation contractors in the United States
problem: Small contractors suffer cash flow strain from slow client payments, lack of deposits, and heavy collection risk and subcontractor payout work.
business_model: Construction payments and project-based working capital, earning fees and financing spread on deposits and payouts

founders.name: Chapman Snowden
founders.background_notes: YC page: 10+ years across finance, venture philanthropy and ed tech. Education not listed on the YC page.

founders.name: Drew Barrett
previous_startups: Companies in real estate, food and beverage and medical (names not listed)
founders.background_notes: Described on the YC page as an entrepreneurial strategist for finance and operations.

technical_complexity.rationale: Payments, deposits, subcontractor payouts and credit underwriting are standard fintech engineering with regulatory and underwriting complexity; the YC page lists 18 people, which suggests a sizable team.

defensibility.rationale: Working capital and payments relationships could create some stickiness among contractors, but financing and payment rails were available to rivals and no proprietary data is documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying the company; the wind-down cause is not public.

market_need_then: A search result on the sector cites a report that 46 percent of contractors struggle with cash flow due to long payment cycles and another that late payments cost construction $64 billion in 2019; both come from undated or later pages and are secondhand.

branding.domain_note: Brand later used go.build per Latka listing; the original company site field in the data is blank.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline: payments for contractors who want to grow (ProToolReviews headline)

rebrands.why: Not stated in sources found; exact date unknown

brand_strength.rationale: Brick was shared by several unrelated startups (a financial API company, a $9M seed company), which confused search results; the rebrand to GoBuild also collides with an Austin company of the same name.

outcome_analysis: YC lists the company as inactive, but no shutdown post-mortem, layoffs or acquisition coverage was found, so the cause is not public. Only a $500K convertible note total is reported by a single database, and the rename from Brick to GoBuild with a team size of 18 suggests the company continued for some time after the batch.
notes: No company website is listed in the directory, so there was no site to fetch. Funding of $500K total with a convertible note rests on a single database (CB Insights) and has no date; stage is set to other because the note is not labeled seed. A Caplight listing shows an Austin real estate company called GoBuild with $3.13M and a seed in Nov 2021; it appears to be a different company and is not recorded as a round. Crunchbase lists a pre-seed for Brick without an amount. Billd is cited with a June 2021 date, a few months after the Winter 2021 batch. Competitor evidence is thin because the search did not return other dated sources. Correction: the Billd competitor was removed because its only source (Product Hunt, 2021-06) is dated after the as_of of 2021-01 and no better dated source was found.
